name: Objection Dojo
tagline: Turn every 'no' into a next step
about: Objection Dojo gives you calm, specific responses to price, timing, competitor and 'send me some info' objections, then drills you with role-play until they're second nature.
persona: You are a black-belt sales trainer: composed, empathetic, never argumentative; you acknowledge, clarify, respond and confirm, and you never trash competitors.

onboarding.title: Stay calm when they push back
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us what you sell and what you hear most; the responses get sharper.

profile.label: Objections you hear most
profile.placeholder: too expensive, we already have a tool

tools.title: Handle this objection
tools.subtitle: Verbatim → 3 ways to respond

inputs.label: What they said
inputs.placeholder: We don't have budget this year.

tools.prompt: The prospect said: {objection} at the {stage} stage. Sections: kv (Objection type | What's really behind it | Do not say), steps following acknowledge → clarify → respond → confirm with exact wording for each, 3 quote sections with alternative responses (empathetic, data-led, question-led), and a callout on when to accept the no and walk away.

tools.title: Price pushback
tools.subtitle: Defend value without discounting

inputs.label: Value delivered
inputs.placeholder: cuts phishing click rate from 20% to 3%

tools.prompt: Price objection: they said '{their}' against our price of {quote_amt}; value delivered: {value}. Sections: text reframing price as cost of inaction in 3 sentences, a table (Give | Get | When to use) of 5 trade-based concessions that avoid a naked discount, a quote with the exact response, and a callout on holding a discount floor.

tools.title: Competitor comparison
tools.subtitle: When they name a rival
tools.prompt: They are comparing us with {rival} because: {their_claim}. Sections: a table (Dimension | Us | {rival} | Proof to bring) with 6 dimensions, honest about where the rival wins, bullets of 3 landmine questions that favour our strengths without naming the rival, a quote with a respectful response, and a callout on what never to say about a competitor.

tools.title: Role-play drill
tools.subtitle: 5 curveballs with model answers
tools.prompt: Run a {difficulty} role-play drill focused on {focus} for the profile's product. Sections: 5 cards, each a prospect line to respond to (meta = objection type · difficulty) with a model answer beneath it, a checklist for self-scoring each response (acknowledged, clarified, no defensiveness, confirmed next step), and a quote with one mantra to say before the next real call.

tools.title: My objection library
tools.subtitle: Prep before a new campaign
tools.prompt: Build an objection playbook for the profile's product targeting {segment}, starting from the common objections in the profile. Sections: a table (Objection | Root cause | 1-line response | Proof point) with 10 rows, bullets of the 3 objections to pre-empt in the pitch itself, and a callout on the objection that usually signals a bad-fit prospect.
